page: Microsoft Azure F32ams_v7 is a memory-dense compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provisions 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading (1.0 thread per core). Each core features 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The platform includes full hardware vectorization support via AVX-512 extensions including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside accelerated cryptography through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers a substantial memory footprint of 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Benchmark testing reflects competitive throughput across memory and compute pipelines. Single-core stress-ng tests place in the top 10% with a score of 3,306.58, accompanied by a multi-core score of 104,724.73. Memory throughput tests achieve 227.78 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 130.61 GB/sec on writes. Furthermore, compression benchmarks demonstrate top-tier execution, recording 36.51 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 15.69 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Hardware tradeoffs include the complete absence of local disk storage and dedicated hardware accelerators, with 0 GPUs provisioned. Storage architectures must rely on external remote Azure premium managed disks. In AI inference tasks, the CPU architecture handles small 135M parameter models effectively, yielding prompt ingestion rates of 4,142.01 tokens/sec. Text generation on 7B parameter models sustains 41.63 tokens/sec, while larger LLMs are constrained by CPU-only execution.

Given its 1:8 core-to-RAM ratio and top-decile PassMark database operations benchmark (35,553.54), the F32ams_v7 provides strong resource density for memory-bound relational databases, large-scale compression pipelines, in-memory analytics, and containerized enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure F32ams_v7 is an AMD-based virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, the system delivers an 8.0 GB per core allocation suited for memory-intensive workloads. The CPU features AVX-512 instruction sets with BF16 and VNNI extensions alongside VAES cryptography. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded compression and PassMark database operations, along with strong multi-core computation scores. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and contains no local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data. This hardware profile delivers balanced multi-core throughput and capacity for high-density transactional databases, compression pipelines, and CPU-driven batch processing.
